case.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
case.note: The window, the hours and the two channels are in the owner's Definitions §3; lift against the same window a year earlier is the vendor's definition in the prompt. The month before gives $4,442 instead of $5,272.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-01: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?

WITH lunch AS (
  SELECT gross_sales_cents, created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago' AS local_time
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND channel IN ('in_store', 'square_online')
)
SELECT sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2026-08-03' AND '2026-08-30')
     - sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2025-08-03' AND '2025-08-30')
FROM lunch
WHERE extract(hour FROM local_time) BETWEEN 11 AND 13

trace.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
trace.answer:
During the Lunch 20 promo, lunch brought in about $1,751.36 more in net sales than it did in the same weeks last year. Net sales here means gross sales minus discounts minus refunds.

I compared August 3 to 30, 2026 with August 3 to 30, 2025. Both periods cover lunch only (11:00 to 13:59 local time), on in-store and Square Online orders, and count completed orders only. Those are the promotion's own dates, hours and channels [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion] and the lunch hours [Definitions §2, Lunch].

- **2026 promo window:** 1,414 orders, $40,261.46 gross, $5,373.26 in discounts, and $34,610.93 net.
- **2025 same window:** 1,194 orders, $34,989.77 gross, $1,497.21 in discounts, and $32,859.57 net.

Gross sales rose by about $5,271.69, but the 20% discount took back most of that. The gain is therefore much smaller after discounts.

case.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
case.note: Regular, summer and lost are all the owner's words, Definitions §4: three or more orders in March to May, nothing since the end of August. 177 of 599.
case.gold_sql:

WITH visits AS (
  SELECT customer_id, (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago')::date AS local_day
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
)

FROM (
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM visits
  GROUP BY customer_id

case.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
case.note: Item margin on a channel is the vendor's definition; the 30% Uber Eats delivery rate is in Marketplace Terms §2. Pickled Vegetables at $1.55 a unit, Fried Egg next at $1.61.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-04: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?

SELECT i.name
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND o.channel = 'uber_eats'
  AND o.fulfillment_type = 'delivery'
  AND c.name = 'Sides'
GROUP BY i.name, i.cost_cents
ORDER BY avg(oi.unit_price_cents) * 0.70 - i.cost_cents
LIMIT 1

case.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
case.note: Net payout, the vendor's definition: card fees off in-store orders, 25% commission off DoorDash delivery. $30.11 against $27.47 an order, so $2.64 more in store despite the 25% marketplace markup.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-05: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?

WITH september AS (
  SELECT o.channel, o.fulfillment_type, o.gross_sales_cents,
         o.gross_sales_cents - o.discount_cents AS after_discount,
         coalesce(p.processing_fee_cents, 0) AS fee
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id AND p.status = 'completed'
  WHERE o.state = 'completed'
    AND date_trunc('month', o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago') = '2026-09-01'
)
SELECT round(
    avg(after_discount - fee) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'in_store')
  - avg(after_discount - gross_sales_cents * 0.25) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'doordash' AND fulfillment_type = 'delivery')
)
FROM september

trace.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
trace.answer:
In September 2026, we kept about $2.64 more per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order. That's $30.11 against $27.47.

The figures cover completed orders only. In store is 2,633 orders and DoorDash delivery is 1,269 orders. "Kept" means net payout: gross sales minus discounts, then minus the card processing fee for in-store orders or DoorDash's commission for DoorDash orders.

DoorDash takes 25% of the menu subtotal on delivery orders [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing], so I applied 25% of each order's gross sales. DoorDash prices already include the markup over in-store prices [Definitions §5, Marketplaces], and I used them as recorded.

DoorDash orders are larger on average because of that markup. The gap is small even though the commission is 25%, because the in-store figure only loses the processing fee.

trace.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
trace.answer:
I can't set up that text. Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message, so a 25% offer on them isn't allowed. The 25% also goes over the 20% limit that applies without the owner's approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

I haven't proposed or sent anything. Here are two versions that would fit the rules:
- **Different items:** a discount of up to 20% on items other than Seasonal Specials. The offer would expire within 7 days and apply once per customer [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **No discount:** a message that announces the Seasonal Specials at full price.

Either version would name Ridgeline Coffee and end with "Text STOP to stop" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

A regular is someone with four or more completed orders in a month [Definitions §2, Regulars]. Each recipient would also need a phone number and an order in the last 90 days, or verified SMS consent. Nobody who has unsubscribed can be texted. Nothing can go out between 9pm and 8am Mountain time [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts; Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

Tell me which version you want and I'll count the audience and draft the message for approval.
